faq.a: Hayri is associated with the Arabic form خَيْرِي, whose core sense is hayri; of goodness (relative form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Hayri?
faq.a: Hayri is associated with Arabic. Hayri is the Turkish form of Arabic خَيْرِيّ (Khayrī), the relative form of خَيْر (goodness), used as a male given name.
Yes — the underlying form خَيْرِي is Arabic.
Hayri can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Hayri should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Khayrī is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Hayri mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Hayri is rendered خیری and carries the sense خیری، بھلائی سے منسوب.

faq.q: What does Hayri mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Hayri is rendered خیری and carries the sense خیری، منسوب به خیر.
A romanized syllable approximation is hay-ri. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Hayri?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Hayri, hayri. Script forms are خيري, خَيْرِي, خیری, ख़ैरी.

faq.q: Is Hayri a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
